answer: Admission by sponsorship moves the cost onto reputation. A new key earns nothing until a seated identity pledges part of its own weight behind it, slashed once the newcomer is caught voting beside another key from the same operator. A sponsor may back only a few keys per epoch, so a farm first needs accounts valuable enough to serve as collateral. Pledging is a lantern over a doorway: it lights the entrant's path and exposes the hand holding it. Fifty aliases admitted in one pattern return a single echo, and each dawn the pledges are rechecked against contradiction reports.
